uncited: - A curvilinear hexahedral mesh (or tetrahedral mesh for degenerate cases).
- Extinction coefficients $K_\nu$ per vertex or cell.
- A 2D image representing the accumulated optical thickness (attenuation) per pixel.
- Final intensity derived from the accumulated attenuation.
- **P-buffer:** A floating-point off-screen buffer (texture) storing the accumulated attenuation sum.
- **Cell Geometry:** Hexahedral connectivity.
- For each hexahedral cell, test if it can be projected as a whole.
- It is non-degenerate (no coinciding vertices).
- If valid, mark it for hexahedral projection.
- Compute the thickness for each vertex of the resulting primitives in software using cell geometry.
- Form a logically circular list of pointers to all cells.
- Render the primitives (triangles) to the P-buffer.
- After rendering a batch of cells, copy the P-buffer to a texture to keep it current for the next iteration.
- After all cells are processed, the P-buffer contains the total optical thickness $\tau$ for each pixel.
- The final intensity is computed from the accumulated attenuation.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of cells, but dependent on the number of rendering passes required to minimize buffer copies.
Subdivision increases the number of primitives.
- **Memory Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of cells for the mesh data.
The P-buffer size is fixed by the image resolution.
Direct projection of hexahedra saves storage and rendering time compared to tetrahedral decomposition.
Parallel accumulation of multiple wavelength bands.
Degenerate or non-convex cells require subdivision, which can introduce small errors.
Buffer copying overhead if many overlapping cells exist.
- **When to use:** Absorption-only radiography (X-ray simulation) where emissivity is negligible.
Suitable for curvilinear hexahedral meshes.
- **When not to use:** Emissive volumes (requires front-to-back compositing).
